questions.q: Why is the family called the first community, and what are its main types?
answer: The family is called the first community because it is the smallest group each person is born into and the first to shape our lives.

answer.text: The family provides care, security, values and a sense of identity, and it is where a child first learns to live with others.

A nuclear family consists of parents and their children; a joint or extended family has several generations and relatives living together; and a blended family is formed when two families come together, for example through remarriage.
Families are changing — nuclear families are becoming more common, especially in cities — but the family remains the basic unit of every community.

questions.q: What is a community, and how do we belong to many communities at once?
answer: A community is a group of people connected by something they share — a place, a language, an occupation, a religion or a common interest.

answer.text: Each person belongs to several communities at the same time: a family, a neighbourhood, a school, a linguistic or religious group, a region and, finally, the nation.
These communities widen outward — from the local village or town, to the region, to the whole country — so that every Indian is part of one large national community.

answer: Belonging to many communities gives us multiple identities that together make us who we are.

questions.q: What values are needed for people to live together peacefully in a community?
answer: Living together in a community depends on shared values that allow different people to get along.

answer.text: Members must work together and share resources and responsibilities, since no one can meet all their needs alone.
People of different religions, languages and customs must respect one another's differences — the spirit of unity in diversity.
Communities work because members depend on one another — farmers, teachers, doctors and cleaners all serve the whole.

answer: With cooperation, tolerance and a sense of duty, a diverse community can live together in harmony.
